## Purpose and runtime
LyricsX is a native macOS lyrics companion (macOS 10.11+) that integrates with music players, finds/downloads timed lyrics, and renders them on desktop, menu bar, and Touch Bar. It is an AppKit/Xcode application with a separate helper target. Project/build entry points are `LyricsX.xcodeproj`, `LyricsX/Supporting Files/Info.plist`, and `LyricsXHelper/Info.plist`.

## Application bootstrap and orchestration
`LyricsX/Component/AppDelegate.swift` is the Cocoa application lifecycle entry point. `LyricsX/Component/AppController.swift` is the likely application-level coordinator for player selection, lyric lifecycle, and presentation controllers. `LyricsX/Component/SelectedPlayer.swift` represents the selected supported music-player integration. This boundary isolates the app from the external MusicPlayer framework.

## Music-to-lyrics pipeline
The core flow is: selected player emits track/playback state → application/controller resolves lyric metadata and lyrics → UI controllers receive current lyric/time updates. LyricsKit supplies remote-source search/download and lyric models; MusicPlayer supplies integrations with supported players. Repo-side metadata/language adaptation lives in `LyricsX/Component/LyricsMetadata+Extension.swift` and `LyricsX/Component/Lyrics+Language.swift`, with Chinese script conversion centralized by `LyricsX/Component/ChineseConverter+Singleton.swift`.

## Display surfaces and synchronized rendering
Lyrics presentation is split by surface:
- Desktop/HUD: `LyricsX/Controller/LyricsHUDViewController.swift`, backed by `LyricsX/View/ScrollLyricsView.swift`.
- Karaoke/timed display: `LyricsX/Controller/KaraokeLyricsController.swift`, `LyricsX/View/KaraokeLyricsView.swift`, and `LyricsX/View/KaraokeLabel.swift`.
- Menu bar: `LyricsX/Controller/MenuBarLyricsController.swift`.
- Touch Bar: `LyricsX/Controller/TouchBarLyricsController.swift` and `LyricsX/Component/TouchBarLyricsItem.swift`.

These controllers are consumers of shared playback/lyric state rather than independent lyric sources. Interactive seeking is represented by the karaoke UI capability described in the README.

## Lyric acquisition and file interchange boundary
Lyrics can be automatically retrieved from external lyric sources through LyricsKit, while `LyricsX/Controller/SearchLyricsViewController.swift` provides user-driven search/selection. Local import/export is a UI boundary using the LRC/LRCX-compatible format; drag-and-drop support is rooted at `LyricsX/View/DragNDropView.swift`. This separates remote lookup from user-supplied lyric files.

## User configuration and lifecycle behaviors
Preferences are hosted by `LyricsX/Controller/Preferences/PreferenceViewController.swift`, with dedicated display, filtering, general, lab, and shortcut panes under `LyricsX/Controller/Preferences/`. Defaults are packaged in `LyricsX/Supporting Files/UserDefaults.plist`. The app also supports player-linked activation/window behavior via `LyricsX/Controller/AutoActivateWindowController.swift`; global shortcuts likely rely on MASShortcut.

## Infrastructure, dependencies, and distribution
Dependencies are resolved through Carthage and Swift Package Manager metadata: `Cartfile`, `Cartfile.resolved`, and `LyricsX.xcodeproj/project.xcworkspace/xcshareddata/swiftpm/Package.resolved`. Material libraries include LyricsKit, MusicPlayer, SwiftyOpenCC, CombineX, SnapKit, MASShortcut, TouchBarHelper, and Sparkle. Update behavior is encapsulated in `LyricsX/Component/Updater.swift` (Sparkle). Localization spans storyboard and app strings under `LyricsX/Base.lproj` and `LyricsX/Supporting Files/* .lproj`; Crowdin configuration is `crowdin.yml`.
